answer: We formalize a Sybil-resistant mechanism where each node commits a dynamic opportunity-cost bond B alongside a zero-knowledge verifiable delay proof. Any adversarial attempt to wander from the protocol's equilibrium via identity multiplication triggers a subgame-perfect slashing penalty S > B, rendering the malicious validation voyage unprofitable. Consequently, the expected utility of generating N Sybil nodes is strictly negative, ensuring that even an ember of honest collateral secures a robust Nash equilibrium.
